title: Exact derived normalization of the ProEtale comparison path
statement: For every commutative ring, chosen Cartesian square and bounded-below input, the ProEtale derived path equals the exact derived image of comparisonSquareProEtalePath, precomposed with comparisonSquareSourceIso.inv and postcomposed with comparisonSquareTargetIso.hom. These paths and endpoint factors are the explicit constructions of [stage3-proetale-comparison-square-paths]. This asserts only one path identification; it assumes and concludes no square coherence. The square is supplied by an IsPullback proof. The assertion is HEq between the derived ordinary path composite and the stated component path, retaining their definitionally equal endpoint presentations to avoid expensive kernel conversion.

proof.text: The private exact_path calculation expands derivation of the three ordinary path factors using mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_trans and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_isoWhiskerLeft/Right. Evaluate these natural-transformation equalities at the input. Three specializations of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_assoc, followed by inverse cancellation, collect the common source and target factors and leave the two exact derived edge comparisons and the exact derived pro-etale square.

The private derive_transport calculation identifies derivation of the equality transport with the transport of total left derived pullback conjugated by its exactness comparisons. Equality induction reduces this to mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_refl and inverse-hom cancellation. The private square_exact calculation expands leftDerivedUpperStarSquareIso, leftDerivedUpperStarComp, leftDerivedFunctorNatIso and leftDerivedFunctorCompIso; cancel the composite exactness comparisons and apply derive_transport. The ordinary proEtaleComparisonComp is definitionally upperStarComp, so mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_trans and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_symm finish the square calculation.

Specialize exact_path to the etale and pro-etale pullbacks and comparison inverse images. The comparisonCoefficientPullbackIso is definitionally comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso.symm. Expand the two leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso components and use square_exact. The bounded-below compatibility is Iso.refl, and the inclusion and lift object equations identify its objects with the unbounded ones. Naturality of the inverse exactness comparison at f-prime moves it across the other edge. Its inverse-hom pair cancels, followed by the mapped inverse-hom pair at g. The remaining two target exactness comparisons are precisely those in comparisonSquareTargetIso. Convert the resulting equality to HEq. No comparison between the etale and pro-etale square paths is used. The fully proved private normalized_path calculation is applied by conversion; unfold only the explicit path and endpoint definitions, identify the ordinary edge comparisons by reflexivity, and associate composites to finish the conversion. This avoids tactic rewriting through partially unfolded endpoint types.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean normalization proof with four fully proved private calculations; endpoint conversion uses the explicit path definitions and associativity. No new holes.

theorem comparisonSquareProEtalePath_normalization
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {X' X Y' Y : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (M : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf Y.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))) :
    HEq
      (comparisonSquareDerivedPath Λ g' f' f g (comparisonSquareProEtalePath Λ
        { toCommSq := sq.toCommSq, isoPullback := sq.isoPullback,
          hom_fst := sq.isoPullback_hom_fst, hom_snd := sq.isoPullback_hom_snd }) M)
      ((leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso f' Λ).hom.app
            (D+(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) g).obj M) ≫
          L(ProEtale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) f').map
            ((leftDerivedUpperStarComparisonIso g Λ).hom.app M) ≫
          (leftDerivedUpperStarSquareIso (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) sq.toCommSq).hom.app
            ((DerivedCategory.Plus.ι ⋙ D(ν^*(Y)[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ])).obj M))
